vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: openclaw-github-assistant
Version: 1.0.4

The OpenClaw GitHub skill is designed to interact with the GitHub API for repository management, issue creation, and CI status checks. It retrieves GitHub credentials (token, username) from environment variables or OpenClaw configuration, which is standard practice. All network calls are directed to the official `https://api.github.com` endpoint. The documentation (`SKILL.md`, `README.md`) clearly outlines required permissions (GitHub PAT with `repo` scope) and provides explicit security warnings regarding token protection. There is no evidence of data exfiltration, malicious execution, persistence mechanisms, or prompt injection attempts against the AI agent. The functionality aligns with the stated purpose, and while it requires high-privilege GitHub tokens, this is necessary for its advertised capabilities.

llm.summary: The skill appears to do what it claims (GitHub repository management), its requested credentials and config are consistent with that purpose, and there are no obvious incoherent or hidden behaviors.

dimensions.detail: Name/description, required env vars (GITHUB_TOKEN, GITHUB_USERNAME), required config keys, and the implemented actions (list repos, create issues, create repos, check CI, etc.) are aligned. No unrelated credentials, binaries, or config paths are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md and index.js limit actions to GitHub API calls and to reading credentials from environment or the OpenClaw config. The SKILL.md's setup instructions (generate a PAT with 'repo' scope and restart the gateway) are consistent with the implemented capabilities, but the recommended 'repo' scope is broad (gives full repo control). The test suite (test.js) will perform live API calls if run, so users should not run it with a high-privilege token on sensitive accounts unless intended.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install/download steps are specified; this is effectively instruction + included JS source. Nothing in the manifest pulls external archives or executes installers.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The only secrets requested are GITHUB_TOKEN and GITHUB_USERNAME, which are appropriate for a GitHub integration. Minor points: GITHUB_USERNAME is redundant because the token can identify the user (index.js falls back to /user). The SKILL.md recommends the 'repo' PAT scope which is appropriate for create_repo and other write actions but is broad — use least-privilege scopes (e.g., public_repo or narrower scopes) if you don't need private-repo or repo-admin actions.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and normal autonomous invocation are set. The skill does not request persistent system-wide privileges or manipulate other skills' configs. Its runtime access is limited to the declared config keys and environment variables.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is consistent with its stated purpose, but before installing: (1) use a least-privilege GitHub token — only grant the scopes you actually need (avoid full 'repo' if you only need public read/write); (2) prefer storing the token in a secrets manager or the OpenClaw config instead of shell profiles on shared machines; (3) be aware the included test.js will make live GitHub API calls if you run it (don’t run tests with a high-privilege token on sensitive accounts); and (4) because the agent can invoke the skill autonomously, consider whether you want an automated agent able to create issues/repos using your token — if not, avoid granting write scopes or disable autonomous invocation for this skill in your agent settings.
